name: Tree Data Structures
description: Master the hierarchical structures and traversal methods essential for efficient data organization and retrieval.

group.definition: The topmost node in a tree structure from which all other nodes descend.
A node in a tree that does not have any child nodes.
The number of edges on the longest path from a specific node to a leaf.
The number of edges from the root node to a specific node.
A tree data structure in which each node has at most two children, typically referred to as the left and right child.
A binary tree where the left subtree contains values less than the parent and the right subtree contains values greater.
A self-balancing binary search tree where the difference in heights of two child subtrees is at most one.
A self-balancing search tree that allows for nodes to have more than two children, optimized for systems with large blocks of data.
A method of visiting nodes where the left subtree is visited first, then the root, and finally the right subtree.
A traversal method where the root node is visited before its child subtrees.
A traversal method where the root node is visited after its left and right subtrees have been processed.
